overview: Reynald of Châtillon was a controversial crusader lord whose aggressive raids and treaty-breaking helped intensify conflict with Saladin before Hattin.
Reynald is remembered as one of the most divisive figures in crusader history: bold to some, reckless and destructive to others.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Reynald of Châtillon was a controversial crusader lord whose aggressive raids and treaty-breaking helped intensify conflict with Saladin before Hattin.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Reynald came from the French knightly world and rose in the Latin East through marriage, military violence, and frontier lordship.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Reynald of Châtillon is remembered as the great villain of the crusader east, a reckless and violent adventurer whose provocations helped bring on the disaster of Hattin. Both Muslim and Christian sources present a brutal, ambitious, and faithless figure — a man who tortured the Patriarch of Antioch, raided into the Arabian heartlands toward the holy cities of Islam, and broke truces by attacking Muslim caravans, outrages that gave Saladin both motive and justification for war.

The Muslim sources regarded him with particular loathing, and the famous tradition of his death holds that Saladin executed him personally after Hattin, having sworn to kill him for his violations — sparing the captured king Guy but striking down Reynald with his own hand. Even the Christian sources, while sometimes admiring his boldness, could not defend his treacheries.

What the record consistently conveys, across hostile traditions, is a figure of exceptional aggression and bad faith, whose provocations were as politically disastrous as they were personally daring. He is remembered as the crusader east's most notorious troublemaker — bold, cruel, and faithless — whose recklessness helped ignite the war that destroyed the kingdom.

contentSections.title: As lord and provocateur
paragraphs: Reynald ruled Antioch by marriage, spent years in captivity, and later controlled Oultrejordain. His raids toward the Red Sea and attacks on caravans made him a direct enemy of Saladin.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: After Hattin in 1187, Saladin personally ordered or carried out Reynald’s execution, while sparing Guy of Lusignan.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Reynald is remembered as one of the most divisive figures in crusader history: bold to some, reckless and destructive to others.
